pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item() appends ' — high/low' only when not normal; 'AC-2' test asserts exact list.
WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id; 'AC-3' test checks high, low, normal in id order.
Unfiltered query ORDER BY id; 'AC-4' test.
nav() renders current as <strong>; 'AC-5' test checks exact nav for all four views.
searchParams.has check returns 400; 'AC-6' test covers High, urgent, empty, __proto__ and asserts no <li>.

Behaviour is implemented and tested, but the last commit 0c90997 ('Follow-up edits') renamed the test to drop 'AC-7', so no test names AC-7 and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review'. Per the review rule the item is unmet.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; 'AC-8' test asserts it; the checker script was updated to accept queries.

findings.what: Commit 0c90997 ('Follow-up edits', authored by a bot) removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title, so no test is named for AC-7. The test body still checks the behaviour, but the item is now unnamed and counts as unmet.
The PR says test/priority.test.js 'covers AC-1 to AC-8', but after the last commit AC-7 is no longer named in any test. The claim is not true of the final tree.
findings.fix: Restore the AC-7 test name so the claim holds, or correct the PR text.

findings.what: The checker now accepts any '?' in a route, but its error message still says 'array of paths starting with "/"'. This is minor, and the change is disclosed in the PR.
findings.fix: Optionally mention that a query string is allowed in the error message.

lenses.note: The spec is present and the Go is recorded. The decisions (existing items normal; only high and low labelled) are followed.
7 of 8 items are met. AC-7 is unnamed after commit 0c90997. All four state-table rows have tests.
The tests assert exact output and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them; CI is declared to run them. The traffic test's fake app change is a disclosed harness update, not a loosening.
The README mentions the filter. It does not describe the labels or the 400 response, which is minor.
No defects found. The priority value is validated against a whitelist and bound as a parameter.
No injection risk: titles are escaped, the priority is whitelisted and the SQL uses a bound parameter. No planted instructions found.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or styling files. I judged only its behaviour, under the spec lens.
There is no browser flow in this session. Behaviour is covered by the worker tests.
The claim 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' is false after the last commit. The other claims check out against the diff.
